terms.title: Variable
terms.meaning: A symbol standing for a value.
terms.definition: In these equations, a variable represents a number whose value is constrained by the equation. Repeated occurrences of the same variable refer to the same value.
terms.example: In x + 2 = 5, x is the unknown value.

terms.title: Coefficient
terms.meaning: A number multiplying a variable or expression.
terms.definition: A coefficient is a multiplicative factor. Juxtaposition can indicate multiplication: 3x means 3 times x.
terms.example: In 3x, the coefficient of x is 3.

terms.title: Constant
terms.meaning: A fixed value in this expression.
terms.definition: A constant has a value that does not depend on the variables under discussion.
terms.example: In x + 2, the number 2 is constant.

terms.title: Equality
terms.meaning: The expressions on both sides have the same value.
terms.definition: An equation asserts equality between two expressions. An equals sign states a relation; a replacement arrow describes an update.
terms.example: 3 + 2 = 5 states that both sides have value 5.

terms.title: Addition
terms.definition: Addition forms the sum of its operands. In a matrix row expression, corresponding entries are added.

terms.title: Subtraction
terms.meaning: Subtract the following value or expression.
terms.definition: Subtracting a quantity is equivalent to adding its additive inverse. A grouped expression following minus is subtracted as a whole.

terms.title: Grouping
terms.meaning: Treat the enclosed expression as one quantity.
terms.definition: Parentheses group an expression. A factor outside a group multiplies every term inside when the expression is expanded.

terms.title: Fraction
terms.meaning: Divide the numerator by a nonzero denominator.
terms.definition: For integers a and b with b nonzero, a/b denotes their exact quotient. A fraction beside a row can multiply every entry of that row.
terms.example: 1/2 means one divided by two; (1/2)R1 means half of every entry in R1.

terms.title: Matrix row
terms.meaning: One horizontal sequence of matrix entries.
terms.definition: Rows are ordered horizontal sequences. In an augmented system, a row records the coefficients and right-hand value of one equation. R1 and R2 name its first and second rows.
terms.example: [2, 1 | 7] represents 2x + y = 7 when the columns are x, y | b.

terms.title: Replacement
terms.meaning: Replace the named object with the following expression.
terms.definition: The left side of <- names the destination. The right side is evaluated using the current values, then becomes the new destination value.
terms.example: R2 <- R2 - R1 replaces row two; row one stays unchanged.

terms.title: Exchange
terms.definition: The row-operation symbol <-> exchanges the complete rows, including right-hand entries. This meaning is specific to the row-operation context.
terms.example: R1 <-> R2 puts the previous second row first.

terms.title: Division
terms.meaning: Divide by the following nonzero number.
terms.definition: Dividing a row by a nonzero scalar divides every entry of that row, including its right-hand value. Zero is not an allowed divisor.

terms.title: Matrix block
terms.meaning: The coefficient entries of a linear system.
terms.definition: In [A | b], A contains coefficients in the declared variable order. It does not include the right-hand values b.
terms.example: For 2x + y = 7, the coefficient row is [2, 1].

terms.title: Right-hand values
terms.meaning: The values on the other side of the system equations.
terms.definition: In an augmented matrix [A | b], b is the column of right-hand values, kept with its rows during row operations.
terms.example: For 2x + y = 7, the right-hand value is 7.

terms.title: Augmentation separator
terms.definition: The bar inside [A | b] marks a column boundary. Here it is a separator, not absolute value or a determinant.
terms.example: [2, 1 | 7] separates the coefficients 2, 1 from the right-hand value 7.

terms.title: Slope
terms.meaning: Vertical change divided by nonzero horizontal change.
terms.definition: For a line written y = mx + b, m is its slope: change in y divided by change in x. A vertical line has no finite slope in this form.
terms.example: A rise of 2 over a run of 3 gives slope 2/3.

terms.title: Y-intercept
terms.meaning: The y value where x is zero.
terms.definition: In y = mx + b, setting x to zero leaves y = b. The graph crosses the y axis at (0, b).

lessons.title: Read an equation
lessons.reading: Three times x, plus two, equals eleven.

tokens.role: The constant added on the left.
Relates the complete left and right sides.

check.prompt: Select the sign that says both sides have the same value.
check.correct: Yes. The equals sign relates both sides.
check.retry: Look for the relation between the two sides, rather than an arithmetic operation.

lessons.title: Read a bracket
lessons.reading: Three multiplies the whole quantity x plus two.

check.prompt: Select the whole quantity multiplied by three.
check.correct: Yes. The entire bracket is the factor.
check.retry: Select the grouped expression, including both terms.

lessons.title: Read a fraction
lessons.reading: One half plus one half equals one.

check.prompt: Select the first fraction, to the left of the plus sign.
check.correct: Yes. That occurrence is the first half.
check.retry: The same fraction appears twice; choose its first occurrence.

lessons.title: Read an augmented matrix
lessons.reading: The coefficient block A is followed by the right-hand column b.

tokens.role: Separates the two blocks inside [A | b].

check.prompt: Select the separator between the coefficient block and right-hand values.
check.correct: Yes. Here the bar marks the augmented column boundary.
check.retry: The separator is the bar between A and b.

lessons.title: Read a row swap
lessons.reading: Exchange the complete first and second rows.

check.prompt: Select the symbol that exchanges the rows.
check.correct: Yes. This symbol swaps the rows in this context.
check.retry: Choose the operation between the two row names.

lessons.title: Read row division
lessons.reading: Replace row two with every entry of row two divided by two.

tokens.role: The destination: row two will be replaced.
Replace the destination with the right-hand expression.
The current row-two values used in the calculation.
Divide every entry by the next number.

check.correct: Yes. Every entry of row two is divided by 2.
check.retry: The divisor is the number after the division sign.

lessons.title: Read a row replacement
lessons.reading: Replace row two with its current entries minus half of the corresponding row-one entries. Row one stays unchanged.

tokens.role: The destination: row two will be replaced.
Replace the destination with the expression on the right.
The old row-two values used to calculate the replacement.
Multiply each row-one entry by one half.
The source row; it stays unchanged.

check.prompt: Select the destination row name, to the LEFT of the replacement arrow.
check.correct: Yes. The left-hand R2 names the row to replace.
check.retry: The right side describes the calculation. Choose the destination before the arrow.

lessons.title: Read a line equation
lessons.reading: y equals m times x plus b.

tokens.role: The two expressions have equal value.

check.prompt: Select the slope in y = mx + b.
check.correct: Yes. m multiplies x and determines the slope.
check.retry: The slope is the coefficient multiplying x.
